topic_summary: Analysis of common law precedent as a contested kernel where the corpus of case law is read through fundamentally different interpretive commitments: strict stare decisis treats precedent as binding backward constraint, while evolutionary frameworks treat it as dynamic normative adaptation. The authority-grounding contest centers on whether judicial legitimacy derives from fidelity to past decisions or responsive evolution to contemporary values.

key_entities: Common Law Precedent Corpus (accumulated case law as authoritative substrate)
Strict Stare Decisis School (binding backward constraint reading)
Evolutionary Jurisprudence School (adaptive normative framework reading)
Litigants (parties subject to precedent application outcomes)
key_tensions: Backward fidelity vs contemporary normative adaptation (interpretive authority grounding)
Stability/predictability vs responsive justice (competing legitimacy claims)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The corpus of common law precedent as accumulated judicial practice, claimed as authoritative substrate for adjudication
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Judicial interpretive legitimacy grounded in either fidelity to past holdings (originalist) or responsive adaptation to evolving norms (living constitutionalism analog for common law)
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Interpretive Custody (Pattern 3) — judiciary holds interpretive monopoly over precedent application, with institutional mechanisms (distinguishing, overruling) that permit controlled revision

readings.commitment: Precedent binds as backward constraint; departure requires extraordinary justification
readings.authority_grounding: Judicial legitimacy derives from fidelity to past authoritative holdings; predictability and equal treatment demand binding force
readings.expected_structural_delta: High constraint rigidity; precedent overruling rare and contested; litigants face narrow pathways for norm challenge; judiciary constrained by accumulated holdings

readings.commitment: Precedent provides adaptive framework; contemporary normative evolution permits reinterpretation
readings.authority_grounding: Judicial legitimacy derives from responsive justice and normative coherence with contemporary values; law must evolve or ossify
readings.expected_structural_delta: Lower constraint rigidity; precedent overruling normalized as corrective; litigants gain broader pathways for norm challenge; judiciary empowered as normative updater

readings.commitment: Precedent weight varies by domain and context; balancing stability and adaptation case-by-case
readings.authority_grounding: Judicial legitimacy requires domain-sensitive judgment; constitutional/statutory precedent treated differently than common law tort; recent precedent more revisable
readings.expected_structural_delta: Medium constraint rigidity with context-dependent variance; precedent hierarchy creates multi-tier extractiveness; litigants face unpredictable domain-switching costs

axiom_contradictions.basis: Strict stare decisis grounds legitimacy in backward fidelity (past holdings as immutable unless demonstrably erroneous), while evolutionary framework grounds legitimacy in forward responsiveness (contemporary norms as legitimating adaptation). No single coherent theory holds both: accepting contemporary norms as sufficient grounds for revision requires rejecting past holdings as necessarily binding.

axes.primary_observable: Overruling rate per decade; judicial rhetoric invoking 'settled law'; dissent frequency in precedent-challenge cases
axes.selection_reason: Core reading with axiom-contradictory relationship to evolutionary_framework; high epsilon from constraint rigidity

axes.structural_delta: Precedent as revisable framework; judicial legitimacy through responsive normative updating to contemporary values

axes.selection_reason: Axiom-contradictory sibling to strict_stare_decisis; captures opposite authority grounding with different victim structure

axes.structural_delta: Precedent weight varies by domain, recency, and institutional context; stability/adaptation tradeoff case-by-case
axes.primary_observable: Differential overruling rates across legal domains (constitutional vs tort vs contract); judicial doctrine distinguishing precedent tiers

omegas.description: Does legislative override (statutory reversal of common law holdings) destabilize all three readings, or does it merely shift the kernel locus from judiciary to legislature? If override is frequent, precedent authority may be piton rather than mountain.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) — legislative override conspicuously absent from extraction

omegas.description: Do transnational citation practices (citing foreign precedent) erode strict stare decisis or enrich evolutionary framework? If judges cite non-binding foreign holdings, does this signal precedent as persuasive rather than authoritative?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) — implicit assumption of national precedent closure

omegas.description: Do machine learning case outcome predictors (trained on precedent corpus) undermine evolutionary framework by exposing precedent as determinate constraint, or validate it by revealing judicial discretion as pattern-breaking adaptation?
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) — legal tech industry benefits from precedent predictability; evolutionary reading threatens that commercial model
